analyticalQuestion: Can retaining input charge in both the active-tail derivative and normalized transport operators certify a substantially larger common analytic radius, and which sufficient inequality becomes limiting?
supportedClaim: For the degree-80 exact center in the active cone q>=-1, 242 fixed input-charge bounds plus one analytic sector covering every s>=241 give the all-order derivative bound 0.68960111886114510073 at r=397/2000. A charge-resolved normalized-transport bound, including the unknown correction, is 0.99941043095132664361<1. The reduced active and normalized transport fields are therefore absolutely analytic on the common isotropic polydisc of radius 397/2000. The old scalar tail and transport bounds fail there. At the nearby probe 199/1000, the present sufficient transport bound is 1.0025428645146803446>1.

variants: four-stage common and fixed-charge radius ladder normalized to R0.31

chartContract.takeaway: Charge resolution raises the common certified radius from 59/500 to 397/2000 and closes the active tail with room to spare; the refined normalized-transport bound is now the binding gate and fails at the nearby 199/1000 control.
chartContract.dataSufficiency: Eight exact radius rows, 242 exact fixed-charge column bounds, one exact analytic large-charge-sector bound, six exact gate values, and four finite exact regression rows. The charge chart is an ordered discrete charge axis, not a time trend, and the infinite-sector diamond is an analytic closure rather than a sampled observation.
